chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abd Allah al-Barqi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:

I described to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) the statement of Hisham al-Jawaliqi, and narrated for him the statement of Hisham ibn al-Hakam: 'He is a body.' He said: 'Verily, nothing resembles Allah. What indecency or foulness is greater than the statement of one who affirms that the Creator of things is a body, or an image, or a created form, or defined, or having limbs? Exalted is Allah from that with a great exaltation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological view on whether God has a physical body?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) refutes the Mu'tazili concept of divine corporeality (jism) by contrasting Hisham ibn al-Hakam’s view with the principle that nothing resembles Him. The Imam argues that attributing physical form, image, or defined limbs to the Creator is a greater indecency than any foul speech, emphasizing God's transcendence above all physical limitations. This hadith is significant in Shia theology for establishing that God is devoid of body and image, and is not composed of parts or attributes that can be compared to creation.
